answer: Every voyage must lock umber on the knoll, a public bonding curve where the n-th live voyage locks (n/100)² umber, refunded only on exit and slashed if judged fake. The knoll counts every live voyage, so clones collide there by raising each other's price: with 1,000 honest voyages a newcomer locks 100 umber, but adding 1,000 clones locks about 233,000 umber, the last alone 400. It breaks if umber can be borrowed cheaply or an attacker out-capitalises the network.
